We need to answer: "What United Kingdom Prime Minister was succeeded in the 1990s by the Leader of the Conservative Party?" The question is ambiguous. Likely asking: Which UK Prime Minister was succeeded (i.e., replaced) in the 1990s by the Leader of the Conservative Party. In the 1990s, the Conservative Party leader became Prime Minister after succeeding a previous PM. In 1990, Margaret Thatcher was succeeded by John Major (who was Conservative Party leader). So the Prime Minister succeeded in the 1990s by the Leader of the Conservative Party: Margaret Thatcher was succeeded by John Major (who was the Conservative Party leader). But the question: "What United Kingdom Prime Minister was succeeded in the 1990s by the Leader of the Conservative Party?" Could also refer to John Major succeeded by Tony Blair (Labour) in 1997, but Blair was not Conservative leader. So likely Thatcher.

We need evidence. Look at evidence: We have "The 1997 Conservative Party leadership election was triggered ... when John Major resigned on 2 May 1997, following his party's defeat at the 1997 general election". That shows John Major was Conservative leader and PM, succeeded by someone else (Tony Blair). Not relevant.

We have evidence about Margaret Thatcher? Not directly. The local elections mention "first annual local elections for the new Conservative Prime Minister Margaret Thatcher." That indicates she was PM in 1980. Not about succession.

We need evidence that Margaret Thatcher was succeeded by John Major in 1990. Not present in given evidence. We have evidence about John Major being Conservative leader since November 1990. That implies he became leader after Thatcher. But we need citation that Thatcher was PM before Major. Not present.

We have evidence about "Major had been Conservative leader and Prime Minister since November 1990." That indicates Major succeeded someone as PM in 1990. The predecessor is Thatcher. But we need citation that Thatcher was PM before Major. Not in evidence.

We have evidence about "The 1997 Conservative Party leadership election was triggered ... when John Major resigned". Not about Thatcher.

Thus we may not have direct evidence for the answer. Could answer "Margaret Thatcher". But need citation. We could cite the local elections sentence: "These were the first annual local elections for the new Conservative Prime Minister Margaret Thatcher." That shows she was PM. But not about succession. We need evidence that she was succeeded by John Major. Not present.

We could answer "Margaret Thatcher" with citation of her being PM, but the question asks which PM was succeeded in the 1990s by the Leader of the Conservative Party. The answer is Margaret Thatcher, succeeded by John Major (who was Conservative leader). We have evidence that John Major was Conservative leader and PM since November 1990. That implies he succeeded Thatcher. But we need citation linking Major's start date to Thatcher's end. Not directly.

We could combine two citations: one showing Major became PM in November 1990, another showing Thatcher was PM before. The first citation: "Major had been Conservative leader and Prime Minister since November 1990." (title "Conservative Party (UK) leadership election, 1997", sentence 1). The second citation: "These were the first annual local elections for the new Conservative Prime Minister Margaret Thatcher." (title "United Kingdom local elections, 1980", sentence 1). That together imply succession. Might be acceptable.

Thus answer: Margaret Thatcher. Provide citations.
